analysis.investment_thesis: Borosil Renewables is a capital-intensive solar glass manufacturer with two consecutive years of net losses (INR -50 Cr in FY24, -87 Cr in FY25), negative ROE of -8.9%, and a P/B of 5.93x — offering no margin of safety whatsoever. The market is pricing in a speculative recovery narrative, which is precisely the kind of story Mr. Market tells when he is in an optimistic mood and demands full — or excessive — payment.
key_strengths: Debt/Equity of 0.23 is manageable — below my 0.5 threshold, and borrowings were reduced from INR 576 Cr (FY24) to INR 203 Cr (FY25)
Revenue has grown consistently from INR 156 Cr (2014) to INR 1,476 Cr (2025), demonstrating genuine business scale
High promoter holding of 58.77% signals owner-operators with skin in the game
key_risks: Negative earnings for two consecutive years (FY24: -50 Cr, FY25: -87 Cr) — fails my absolute requirement of 3-5 years of uninterrupted positive earnings
EBITDA has collapsed 71% from INR 256 Cr (FY22) to INR 73 Cr (FY25) despite revenue growing — severe margin compression from cost pressures
Free cash flow has been negative in 4 of the last 5 years, with capex consuming cash relentlessly (INR -373 Cr in FY22, -348 Cr in FY23)
red_flags: Graham Number is incalculable — EPS is negative, meaning the stock fails the most basic quantitative screen
P/B of 5.93x is nearly 4x my maximum acceptable ratio of 1.5x — you are paying INR 6 for every INR 1 of book value
Finance costs have quintupled from INR 6 Cr (FY19) to INR 32 Cr (FY25) while operating income fell from INR 109 Cr to INR 58 Cr — interest coverage has deteriorated sharply
No dividends — the company returns nothing to shareholders while destroying book value through losses
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my standpoint, Borosil Renewables fails on virtually every quantitative criterion I have established over decades. The P/E of 73.3x is reported on some trailing basis, but the reality is the company earned INR -87 Cr in FY25 — there is no earning power to value. P/B at 5.93x means the market is paying a dramatic premium over net assets with no demonstrated ability to earn a return on those assets (ROE: -8.9%, ROCE: -4.41%). The operating margin of 25.84% is flattering window-dressing; it evaporates once one accounts for depreciation, interest, and the full cost structure, yielding a net loss.

The historical record is instructive and alarming. EBITDA peaked at INR 256 Cr in FY22 and has since declined to INR 73 Cr in FY25 — a 71% collapse — while revenue grew 130%. This tells me the business is caught in a commodity price squeeze: solar glass prices globally have been decimated by Chinese overcapacity, and Borosil is a price-taker in an industry where the competition is subsidized state enterprise. The consistently negative free cash flow (four of the last five years) means this business consumes more capital than it generates. An intelligent investor demands proof of earning power before paying anything above liquidation value — here, one is being asked to pay INR 6,986 Cr for a business that lost INR 87 Cr last year. I see no margin of safety; I see only speculation.
